analysis:
Alphabet fell 2.9%, slightly better than the 3.3% median drop among its mega-cap tech peers, in a session where the broader market (SPY down 4.4%) sold off sharply. The coverage includes a Wall Street Journal headline about a historic tech stock rout and "$2.5 trillion AI reality check," while another piece discusses the Nasdaq correction; a third headline mentions Google's plans for a $17 billion Wyoming data center, and there's a dip-buying analysis noting Alphabet leads on RSI among Mag7 stocks. 

The stock reported eight days ago on October 28, missing estimates by 29.5% and dropping 12.6% the following session — an abnormal move of 12.1 points beyond what the market's direction would have predicted, one of the most severe reactions in its recent history. Across the last eight reports, Alphabet has typically moved 3.6 percentage points beyond the market around earnings, and while it beat estimates seven times, one of those beats was followed by a negative abnormal move, showing that surpassing forecasts hasn't guaranteed upside.
